    About this practice table

    Opponents use simple, varied play styles. This is practice for the flow of the game, not solver-grade strategy.

    Fixed blinds. Empty stacks refill between hands. Progress is saved in this browser only; it does not sync between devices.

    Start a fresh session?

    Your current hand and chip stacks will be replaced. Everyone starts with 2,000 chips.

    Quick reference

    What do the actions mean?
    Fold
    Leave this hand. Chips you already put in stay in the pot.
    Check
    Stay in without adding chips. Only available when there is no bet to match.
    Call
    Match the current bet, or put in your remaining chips if you have less.
    Bet / raise
    Put chips in first, or increase the amount others must match. “Raise to” is your total for this betting round.
    How does a hand work?

    Everyone gets two private cards. Betting starts left of the big blind. Three shared cards (the flop), then one (the turn), then one (the river) follow, each with a betting round.

    After the flop, action starts left of the dealer button. At showdown, make your best five-card hand using any combination of your two cards and the five shared cards. You can also win when everyone else folds.

    D = dealer button. SB / BB = small / big blind: forced starting bets that rotate each hand.

    Hand rankings, strongest first
    1. Straight flush
    2. Four of a kind
    3. Full house
    4. Flush
    5. Straight
    6. Three of a kind
    7. Two pair
    8. One pair
    9. High card

    Ace can be high or low in a straight: A–2–3–4–5 is the lowest. Suits never break a tie.
